course_title: Clinical and Dermatoscopic Diagnosis in Skin Cancer Practice

learning_outcomes.description: Apply clinical and dermatoscopic principles and lesion recognition techniques in diagnosing skin cancer.
Analyse and evaluate dermatoscopic patterns to inform diagnostic pathways and refine clinical reasoning.
Demonstrate awareness of public health issues and collaborative practice in skin cancer prevention.
Integrate cultural and social awareness in dermatoscopic assessments, particularly for underserved communities.
Present and explain dermatoscopic findings clearly and accurately to peers and patients.
Model ethical, accurate documentation and decision-making in dermatoscopic practice.

assessments.task_description:
You will produce a portfolio of 5 (five) cases of skin lesions (benign and malignant melanocytic, benign and malignant keratinocytic, inflammatory, adnexal, other malignant, vascular, infiltrates, etc). Each case will require a positional, clinical close-up (macro) and dermatoscopic photo of the lesion, a provisional and differential diagnosis and a copy of the histopathology report (where applicable). Then, a short list including incidence, clinical features (typical size and distribution, shape, border, colour, surface features), dermatoscopic features (pattern, colours, and clues), and any associations. This information will need to cite the limited references used to compile the information. The portfolio will be due by the end of Week 10.

Inadequate or suboptimal photos and/or poor dermatoscopic assessment result in a mark of less than 7/10.

The overall mark for the portfolio will constitute 20% of the final grade.

assessments.task_description:
One Final Examination to be administered online during the examinations period.

The specific date and time of the examination will be notified on Learn.UQ.

The exam will contain:

  • Multiple Choice and True/False questions
  • Questions designed to test basic knowledge covered in the scope of the course; and
  • Questions designed to test your ability to utilise the knowledge that you have learned.
  • There will be images of skin lesions, both clinical as well as dermatoscopic that will form the basis of questions.
  • There will be histopathology images of skin lesions that will form the basis of questions.

learning_activities.topic:
Weekly Zoom Meeting

An online tutorial meeting via Zoom. The meeting will be hosted by the course co-ordinator and lecturers and will at times include a guest lecturer. The meeting schedule will be posted on Learn.UQ. This will be a forum for discussing the previous week's material and new clinical cases. The focus is to refine your dermatoscopic assessment of skin lesions.

It is planned that these meetings will be recorded for the benefit of those who may be unable to join the meeting in real time.
